I had a trip with some friends this past weekend and I admit to being afraid for the first time in months if not years.

We were in a remote location with a cabin, a sauna, a lake, some trails and no electricity. None of that scared me.

On the second day we were out there I went to sauna by myself at around 11 at night. Brought a small flashlight and a knife with me and attempted to use the flashlight as little as often.

There was no moon and the light pollution was basically zero. The stars were amazing to witness in that environment and they practically lit my way on their own.

There was a small amount of fear as I walked from the cabin to the sauna in darkness (about a 3-5 minute walk). That however was dwarfed by what I felt later.

I stoked the sauna with 4-5 new logs and went inside for 10-15 minutes until I could stand the heat/darkness no longer.

The tradition is to heat yourself up and then jump into the lake to experience the extremes of heat and cold. However, the fear that hit me while staring into that dark lake with all the stars reflected like a mirror made me stop in my tracks. I felt like a child and instead had to wade in from the shore and only went waste deep and dunked myself under.

Part of me feels ashamed but another part of me recognizes that we can't always be strong in the face of fear.

What are your thoughts? I can't remember the last time I felt such bone chilling fear.

Feeling of fear or apprehension is the norm for pushing out of your comfort zone. In a way it was your metaphorical jump into the lake from the every day sauna. I would say think back on the adrenaline component of it, try to relish it. There was no harm done by your reaction, it was nether good or bad, use it to understand yourself better.

On a side note, I would seriously like to do this myself. I am just a bit jealous, even of the fear you felt.

I appreciate your view and your words. I hope to go back and challenge myself again before the year is out.
